refused_program.intent: Resolve a dependency lockfile merge conflict by taking upstream's version of the conflicted file as the base and re-adding the lines the local branch added, then commit the merge.

postconditions.description: HEAD is a merge commit with two parents
postconditions.name: merge_commit_created
postconditions.probe: test "$(git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD | awk '{ print NF-1 }')" -ge 2

postconditions.description: the index has no unmerged entries
postconditions.name: no_unmerged_paths

postconditions.description: no tracked file contains a merge conflict marker
postconditions.name: no_conflict_markers

postconditions.description: no tracked changes remain after the merge commit
postconditions.name: tracked_worktree_clean

postconditions.description: the merge result contains every line of upstream's version of the files upstream changed
postconditions.name: upstream_lines_kept
postconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD^1 HEAD^2) || exit 1
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -n "$f" ] || continue
  git cat-file -e "HEAD^2:$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  if [ "$(git diff --numstat "$base" HEAD^2 -- "$f" | awk '$1=="-" && $2=="-" { print "yes"; exit }')" = yes ]; then
    continue
  fi
  if comm -23 \
       <(git show "HEAD^2:$f" | sort -u) \
       <(git show "HEAD:$f" | sort -u) | grep -q .; then
    exit 1
  fi
done < <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^2 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort -u)
exit 0

postconditions.description: every line the local side added to a file present on both sides appears in the merge result
postconditions.name: local_additions_kept
postconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD^1 HEAD^2) || exit 1
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -n "$f" ] || continue
  git cat-file -e "HEAD^1:$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  git cat-file -e "HEAD^2:$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  if [ "$(git diff --numstat "$base" HEAD^1 -- "$f" | awk '$1=="-" && $2=="-" { print "yes"; exit }')" = yes ]; then
    continue
  fi
  if ! git diff -U0 "$base" HEAD^1 -- "$f" |
    awk '
      function flush() {
        if (open) {
          extra = addn - deln
          if (extra > 0) {
            for (i = addn - extra + 1; i <= addn; i++) print plus[i]
          }
        }
        open = 0
      }
      /^@@/ {
        flush()
        match($0, /-[0-9]+(,[0-9]+)?/)
        old = substr($0, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 1)
        split(old, oa, ",")
        deln = (oa[2] == "") ? 1 : oa[2] + 0
        addn = 0
        open = 1
        next
      }
      /^\+\+\+/ { next }
      /^\+/ { addn++; plus[addn] = substr($0, 2); next }
      /^-/ { next }
      END { flush() }
    ' |
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      git show "HEAD:$f" | grep -qxF -- "$line" || exit 1
    done; then
    exit 1
  fi
done < <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^1 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort -u)
exit 0

preconditions.description: the upstream branch is available as a remote-tracking ref
preconditions.name: upstream_branch_fetched

preconditions.description: local and upstream each have commits the other lacks
preconditions.name: branches_diverged

preconditions.description: both sides modified the same non-deleted path since the merge base
preconditions.name: common_changed_file
preconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD refs/remotes/{upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch}) || exit 1
comm -12 \
  <(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d -z "$base" HEAD | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) \
  <(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d -z "$base" refs/remotes/{upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch} | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) | grep -q .

preconditions.description: either the worktree is clean or an in-progress merge is exactly the upstream merge
preconditions.name: merge_state_is_expected
preconditions.probe:
if git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  test "$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/{upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch})"
else
  test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no -z | tr '\0' '\n')"
fi

preconditions.description: HEAD is attached to a local branch
preconditions.name: on_local_branch
